candidate.title: A changed file with a non-ASCII or special-character name silently drops out of the ticket-scoped hunt
candidate.description: In a ticket-scoped hunt, changedFiles reads `git diff --name-only` without -z and without disabling core.quotepath. Git prints a changed path that holds a non-ASCII byte, a double quote, a backslash or a control character as a quoted, escaped string. The preflight then keeps only names for which existsSync(join(repoDir, name)) is true. The quoted string is not a path on disk, so the file is dropped with no note or count. The author of the audited branch controls file names. A changed file with such a name is absent from the SCOPE file: lines, the file count, the lane decisions and the Cloudflare `scope_paths`, so the hunt's verdict can describe a change set that omits that file.
candidate.claimed_root_cause: The path list is parsed from newline-separated git output that quotes unusual names, and an existence filter then discards what it cannot resolve, silently and without -z.

trace.description: git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d <base>...<branch> is spawned with no -z and no -c core.quotepath=false, so names with unusual bytes are quoted by git.
stdout is split on newlines and kept as the list of changed paths, quoted forms included.
The list is filtered by existsSync(join(repoDir, f)); a quoted name does not exist on disk, so the file is removed from the scope with no note.
Only the surviving names are printed as SCOPE file: lines, which the overlay uses as the run's scope_paths, so the omitted file is never audited.

evidence.description: childEnv adds only NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath on Windows and sets no git quoting configuration.
The tests check hostile names in manifest cells; none puts a quoted-name file in a ticket change set.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run and the preflight was not run, so git's quoting of such a name in a ticket-branch diff was not observed.
Whether the user's or system git config sets core.quotepath=false is a deployment fact outside source; the default is true.

validation_plan.local: In a dummy repository, commit a file named with a non-ASCII character or a double quote on a ticket branch and run hunt-preflight.mjs for that ticket. Confirm the file is missing from SCOPE file: lines and from the count. Then compare against `git diff --name-only -z`. Fix: pass -z (or -c core.quotepath=false and a literal parse), split on NUL, and report a changed path that does not exist on disk in a note instead of dropping it.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner may run git config --get core.quotepath on the machines that run hunts to see whether the default has been changed.

checks.invariant: Every file the ticket's change set touches appears in the SCOPE file: lines, whatever the file is named
checks.result: changedFiles runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d <base><sep><branch>` with no -z and no -c core.quotepath=false (hunt-preflight.mjs:505). childEnv adds nothing git-related (resolve-tool.mjs:56-58). Git quotes such names by default: a path with a non-ASCII byte, a double quote, a backslash or a control character is printed as a double-quoted C-escaped string. The result is split on newlines (:506) and then filtered with existsSync(join(repoDir, f)) (:580). A quoted name is not a path on disk, so it is dropped with no note and no count. The rendered file: lines (:625), the SCOPE file count, the lane decision from `files.length` (:408-409) and the `scope_paths` of the Cloudflare run all omit that changed file. A ticket-scoped hunt (the default depth is quick) can then report on a change set that leaves out the file the author named in a non-ASCII way. Full-audit mode uses walk() and is not affected. Not observed: the sandbox is unavailable and the preflight was not run.

checks.invariant: A ref or branch name that reaches git argv, and the review-preflight output that carries ranges, cannot be read as an option or forge a range
checks.result: The base is repos[].defaultBranch from the config (qa-preflight.mjs:266, default 'main'). It goes unvalidated into the argument `${base}...${branch}` with no `--` or --end-of-options (hunt-preflight.mjs:505; the same shape is in qa-preflight.mjs:224-237). A base starting with `--output=` would be taken as git's --output option and write the name list to a file whose name ends in `...<branch>`. The suffix keeps it from naming a useful file, so the impact is nil and this is hardening only. The branch half comes from rev-parse and is filtered by the ticket regex, and it is not in an option position. The ticket id passed to bash is validated (no leading '-', no whitespace, hunt-preflight.mjs:530). A forged RANGES section cannot come from DOCS: the awk filter in review-preflight.sh:36 prints only lines of the form `<n> bytes`. One side effect: ticketRanges aborts on any line containing 'ERROR' anywhere in review-preflight output (hunt-preflight.mjs:483), so a doc path containing that word stops the hunt. That is fail-closed.
